Source: GRETIL. Lore: sandeśa-kāvya, Abhinava vivṛti (KSTS 67). ## 2. The argument, reconstructed step by step

**Clouds make travelers long (v.19):** *utkaṇṭhayanti pathikān jaladāḥ svanantaḥ* — clouds
thundering make travelers long. The cloud (jalada) is the messenger; its thunder (svananta)
awakens longing (utkaṇṭhā) in the traveler (pathika). The rasa's vibhāva is now the cloud
itself. **Sorrow grows (v.19 cont.):** *śoko vivardhati ca tadvinatāsv anantaḥ* — sorrow grows in
those, endless. The vinatā (those bent low, the humbled) are the separated lovers; their
sorrow (śoka) grows without end (ananta). **Love-festival (v.20):** *ratyutsavaṃ priyatamaiḥ saha mānayanti* — they honor the
love-festival with beloveds. The lovers (priyatama) celebrate (mānayanti) the festival of
love (ratyutsava) together — the rasa's anubhāva is communal, not solitary. **Cloud-arrival (v.20 cont.):** *meghāgamaṃ priyasakhi śvasamānayanti* — cloud-arrival, dear
friend, they bring. The cloud's arrival (meghāgama) is brought (śvasamānayanti) by the dear
friend (priyasakhi) — the messenger is delivered. **The tribute (v.21):** *jīyeya yena kavinā yamakaiḥ pareṇa* — may I be conquered by which
poet, by yamakas, other. The poet (kavi) who conquers by yamakas (the figure of speech
where the same word is used twice with different meaning) is the better poet. The speaker
yields to that skill. **The offering (v.21 cont.):** *tasmai vaheyam udakaṃ ghaṭakarpareṇa* — to him I pour water
in ghaṭakarpara. The offering (udaka, water) in the potsherd (ghaṭakarpara) is the tribute:
the speaker pours water for the poet who surpassed him. ## 3. Unresolved / uncertain (not invented)
